## Answer: $2024^{4046}$

**Reduction to a graph problem.** Model the grid as a bipartite graph with one vertex per row and one per column. Each black square $(r,c)$ becomes an edge joining row $r$ to column $c$.

- **A cycle gives a non-simple coloring.** A cycle $r_1 c_1 r_2 c_2 \dots r_k c_k r_1$ in this graph has distinct rows and columns. The corners $(r_i,c_i)$ are black. The ant can walk along row $r_i$ to column $c_i$, turn there, walk along column $c_i$ to row $r_{i+1}$, turn, and so on. Each turn happens on a black square, and consecutive segments are perpendicular, so no 180° reversal is needed. The ant returns to its starting corner.
- **Non-simple implies a cycle.** Any closed walk the ant can make with turns only on black squares traces a closed rectilinear polygon whose corners are black squares. The corners alternate between sharing a row and sharing a column, so they give a closed trail in the bipartite graph. A closed trail with no repeated corners contains a cycle.

So a coloring is simple exactly when its black-square graph is a forest.

**Maximality.** A maximal forest in $K_{n,n}$ (with $n = 2024$) must be a spanning tree: if it missed a vertex, or had two components, some edge of $K_{n,n}$ could be added without creating a cycle. Conversely, every spanning tree is maximal, since adding any other edge of $K_{n,n}$ closes a cycle.

**Counting.** The number of spanning trees of $K_{m,n}$ is $m^{n-1} n^{m-1}$. With $m = n = 2024$:

$$2024^{2023} \cdot 2024^{2023} = 2024^{4046}.$$

ANSWER: $2024^{4046}$
